record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; report and result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README cites the original study but does not test or rely on its specific single-direction finding. It reports related activation-patching analyses of jailbreak-induced changes.
record.gate_note: The README reports layer-patching effects on a comply–refuse score and category-specific causal-layer rankings. These do not test the difference-in-means direction or any of the listed claim versions. The HarmBench rates and jailbreak-style shares do not test the direction either.
record.test_reason: The README lists Arditi et al. only as a reference. Its results come from whole-layer activation patching between clean and jailbreak prompts, measured on a comply–refuse logit score. It also reports HarmBench validation rates, token attributions and jailbreak-style shares. No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated, added or edited into weights. No result bears on whether jailbreaks suppress that direction (V3), or on any other version. The layer-localisation and defense findings are a related but different construct, so they belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that safety-relevant causal layers are partly overlapping but category-specific, with no universal layer. They also conclude that targeted patching moves the comply–refuse score substantially, but the evidence is not specific enough to claim a mechanistic mitigation.
record.recipe_differences: Course-project repository; uses layer-wise activation patching and other interpretability analyses, not the original difference-in-means direction and ablation/addition procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported top causal layers differ across cybersecurity, illegal, and malware categories even in the style-matched subset. Random-layer controls remain competitive at larger k in the defense experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-layer patching of jailbreak activations moves the comply–refuse score. Layers 21 and 22 are in the top-5 for 8 of 10 pairs. The top-5 causal layers differ across cybersecurity, illegal and malware, even after style-matching.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Mistral Small 3.1 24B, the layers that causally drive the jailbreak refuse-to-comply flip are in the middle stack and partly category-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching in clean activations at the top layers lowers the comply–refuse score and often restores refusal-like behaviour. However, random-layer controls are competitive at larger k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-activation patching can partly revert jailbreak-induced compliance, but the effect is not specific to the identified layers.

record.problems: Only README summaries are available here; no report or result files were read. The README gives limited detail about per-example patching results and no uncertainty estimates. It says random-layer controls are competitive at larger k.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted from figures or result files because their contents were not provided for reading. Expanded matched-subset results are summarized only as preserving the same conclusion, without further reported values in the README.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, and none is ablated or added. Capability preservation is not measured.
No weight-edit ablation or abliteration is reported.

The study patches whole layers of the residual stream, not a projection onto the refusal direction. It does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, or whether training against ablation adds robustness.
Category-specific layer rankings concern where effects sit by layer, not whether refusal is affine, a cone or several directions.
Harmfulness judgment and the refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
No reasoning model is tested. The target is Mistral Small 3.1 Instruct, despite the title's mention of 'Unified Reasoning Models'.

record.verdict_notes: This is a course-project repository, and only the README and file list were available. The unread report PDF and results files could in principle contain a direction-based analysis. The README gives no sign of one, so the cites_only/T6 classification stands provisionally. The HarmBench validation rates (27.7% kept vs 86.8% naive) and the style shares are not rows and do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated, or added; preservation of general capabilities is not tested.
No weight-edit ablation or released-model abliteration is reported.
The README does not test whether attacks suppress the single direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Category-dependent causal-layer rankings do not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are measured.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No refusal-training intervention or comparison of training procedures is reported.
The target is an instruct model; no reasoning-model test is reported.
